bull.b: The large installed base creates an expanding foundation for recurring instruments, accessories, and service revenue. With recurring revenue already representing most sales, continued system placements and procedure growth can improve revenue visibility and support durable customer relationships.

bull.t: Strong Cash Generation and Balance Sheet
bull.b: Strong free cash flow and substantial liquidity give Intuitive flexibility to fund research, product development, customer support, and expansion without relying heavily on debt. This financial resilience can help sustain investment through changing procedure volumes and capital-spending conditions.

Ongoing product upgrades and regulatory submissions broaden Intuitive’s technology platform beyond its established systems. Progress in visualization, workflow, training, and additional robotic applications can support adoption across specialties and care settings over the medium term.

bear.b: Weak tender activity and stronger domestic competition constrain system placements in China, while policy-driven pricing pressure can reduce the economics of that market. The lack of da Vinci 5 clearance there also limits the near-term product opportunity and regional growth contribution.

bear.t: Extended-Use Instruments May Reduce Recurring Revenue
bear.b: The extended-use program could improve customer economics and support adoption, but it may also reduce replacement frequency or revenue per procedure for instruments and accessories. Because the company has not quantified the effect, recurring-revenue durability remains exposed to rollout and utilization outcomes.

A slower growth profile can make it harder to absorb rising operating expenses and input costs through scale. Although profitability remains strong, continued deceleration would reduce operating leverage and place greater importance on sustained procedure growth, placements, and disciplined spending.
